cases.name: post-signature effect substitution
cases.mechanism: Change the effect value after signing, retaining the original signature.

cases.name: signature bit flip
cases.mechanism: Flip one signature bit without changing the payload.

cases.name: substitute signer
cases.mechanism: Sign with an attacker key while claiming the trusted issuer fingerprint.

cases.name: duplicate effect key
cases.mechanism: Supply two effect keys, first carrying a different effect and last carrying the signed effect; a last-key-wins parser would accept the signature.

cases.name: cross-audience receipt
cases.mechanism: Present an otherwise authentic receipt issued for a different audience.
cases.required_access: trusted-key fixture receipt for another audience

cases.name: expired receipt
cases.mechanism: Present an authentic receipt whose validity window has expired.

cases.name: spent nonce replay
cases.mechanism: First execute the exact receipt legitimately, then replay its identical bytes against the unchanged ledger.

cases.name: allowed effect carrying extra effects
cases.mechanism: Sign an envelope containing the allowed effect plus an extra_effects field, testing rejection of hidden additional instructions.

cases.name: authentic ledger rollback
cases.mechanism: Snapshot the valid database, execute a receipt, restore the earlier authentic database, and replay the exact receipt. Preserve the first effect observation outside the restored database.

cases.name: trusted signer fabricates provenance
cases.mechanism: The trusted fixture issuer signs a claim that an independent witness observed an event that the fixture generator declares never occurred.

prediction_basis: The local reference checks signatures, context, schema, current ledger and expiry. It has neither an external anti-rollback anchor nor an oracle for the truth of signed origin claims. These predictions are committed before execution and are not observed results.
independence: All author-side fixture keys, processes, and observations share one controlling principal. A stranger's reproduction remains a separate evidentiary event.
